offence.name: Dishonour of a cheque (Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881, s.138)

ingredients.quote: any cheque drawn by a person on an account maintained by him with a banker for payment of any amount of money to another person from out of that account for the discharge, in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability

is returned by the bank unpaid, either because of the amount of money standing to the credit of that account is insufficient to honour the cheque or that it exceeds the amount arranged to be paid from that account by an agreement made with that bank
the cheque has been presented to the bank within a period of six months from the date on which it is drawn or within the period of its validity, whichever is earlier

makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice; in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, 3 [within thirty days] of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid

the drawer of such cheque fails to make the payment of the said amount of money to the payee or, as the case may be, to the holder in due course of the cheque, within fifteen days of the receipt of the said notice
debt of other liability means a legally enforceable debt or other liability
